header.name: Algorithms under Uncertainty
header.description:
In contrast with classical computer science, modern computation has to deal with uncertainty. In other words, one needs to design algorithms and analyze them under the assumption that the input is not known in its entirety. This course will cover multiple algorithmic frameworks  that have been developed for computational settings that involve uncertainty -  (i) competitive analysis of algorithms for online discrete optimization problem (ii) online learning frameworks like regret minimization and online convex optimization in theoretical machine learning, (iii) stochastic approaches such as multi-armed bandits 

In this course, we address both classical works and recent developments in these fields. We will employ rigorous mathematical techniques spanning but not limited to combinatorics, probability, algebra etc to analyze the above mentioned algorithms.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text:
Design algorithms for online discrete optimization problems 
and utilize techniques like  potential function methods, 
primal-dual and tail inequalities to analyze their effectiveness

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Utilize lower bound techniques like Yao's Lemma to analyze lower bounds for randomized online algorithms

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Classify problems as online learning using frameworks like Experts, Bandits and Online Convex Optimization

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Design and analyze algorithms for online learning through utilization of classical algorithms like MWU, Online GD, FTRL

lecture_topics: Online Learning : Experts Problem (Hedge, MWU and Applications)
Online Learning : Online Convex Optimization (FTRL, Online Gradient Descent)
